title: SMOKE / FUMES / AVNCS SMOKE

alert.trigger: Flight or cabin crew suspect smoke/fumes from the avionics, the air conditioning or the cabin equipment; the AVIONICS SMOKE alert triggers; or there is a smell of smoke/fumes in the cockpit. For another ECAM SMOKE alert (cargo, lavatory), apply the ECAM first.

effectivity.note: The QRH lines are the same for all HS-TX. Only the FCOM STATUS after a smoke ELEC EMER CONFIG differs slightly.

summary: Time is critical: red LAND ASAP, and be prepared to divert immediately. Immediate actions protect the crew, stop further contamination and open communication with the cabin. If the source is not immediately isolated, start the diversion and the descent to FL 100 / MEA-MORA. Then identify the source: air conditioning, cabin equipment, or avionics/electrical. At any time after the immediate actions, consider REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMES, ELEC EMER CONFIG or an immediate landing.

background.text: This procedure includes all the steps of the AVIONICS SMOKE procedure.

The immediate actions are common to all cases of smoke or fumes, whatever the source. Their objectives are flight crew protection, avoiding further contamination of the cockpit/cabin, and communication with the cabin crew.
A diversion may be avoided if the source is obvious, accessible and extinguishable, or confirmed isolated after the immediate actions.

Guidelines for the source: smoke/fumes first from the ventilation outlets, or detected in the cabin, suggest air conditioning, and several SMOKE alerts will follow shortly (apply the ECAM procedures). After an ENG or APU failure they may come through the bleed system and recirculate until they disappear. Only the AVIONICS SMOKE alert suggests avionics. Smoke while an equipment is declared faulty suggests that equipment.
A smell of smoke/fumes similar to orange peels: suspect a toxic leak of rain repellent fluid. Similar to pine needles: suspect a non-toxic leak.
With VENTILATION BLOWER and EXTRACT both in OVRD, a single pack may not be able to maintain the cabin pressure. Restore normal configuration if PACK 2 is not suspected to cause smoke/fumes.
CARGO AFT ISOL VALVE OFF prevents a cargo smoke warning from being triggered by cabin smoke.

Partial shedding was removed from the procedure: shedding one side and then the other with a battery charging leaves DC 1, DC 2 and the BAT bus bars inoperative for the rest of the flight. Full ELEC EMER CONFIG lets the crew recover the normal electrical configuration for landing, particularly normal braking.
EMER ELEC GEN 1 LINE OFF opens the GEN 1 line contactor: GEN 1 keeps running and supplies one fuel pump in each wing tank, and AC BUS 1 is supplied by GEN 2 through the bus tie contactor.

technique.text: An immediate diversion should be considered as soon as smoke/fumes are detected. If the source is not immediately obvious, accessible and extinguishable, initiate it without delay.

The boxed items may be applied at any time in the procedure, but not before the immediate actions. After the first steps of REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMES, come back here for the suspected source while descending to FL 100; reaching FL 100, complete REMOVAL OF SMOKE / FUMES.
Remain in ELEC EMER CONFIG until a late stage, and restore some generation a few minutes before landing.
Coordination with the cabin crew is a key element.

values.HS-TXA..TXO: Lists CTR TK FUEL UNUSABLE; ENG 1+2 N1 DEGRADED MODE marked "IAE-powered aircraft"
values.HS-TXP..TXU: No CTR TK FUEL UNUSABLE line; no IAE marking

gaps.text: The QRH line "CKPT / CAB COM" names no pilot; the PF is shown because the PF communicates, confirmed by the user. The PM is shown for the panel lines as read & do.
The HS-TO-only version (QRH 27.01A, FCOM P 19–27/50) is excluded, including its PACK (AFFECTED SIDE) line.

The manuals have no paragraph specific to smoke in the aft cabin. Cabin smoke is treated by the suspected source, confirmed by the user: FCTM says smoke/fumes detected in the cabin may suggest AIR COND, otherwise CABIN EQPT.
FCOM and QRH line wording differs slightly (OXY MASK / GOGGLE, CKPT / CABIN COM, "within 5 min"). The brief quotes the QRH.
